mainTopic: A woman seen with her ex-husband after a גט (זנות or קידושין), and the status of a woman whose גט takes effect only if her husband dies.
overview: This amud opens with the end of a משנה about a husband who gives a גט that works only if he dies from his illness. רבי יהודה says that until then she is a full אשת איש, and רבי יוסי says her status is in doubt. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא about a divorced woman seen alone with her ex-husband, asking whether we worry about זנות or about new קידושין. רב נחמן, אביי and רבא each read the ברייתא differently. After each reading, the גמרא asks which opinion fits רבי יוחנן's rule that the dispute about a second גט applies only when the couple was seen having relations. Under רב נחמן's reading the rule fits everyone. Under אביי's reading it fits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Under רבא's reading it fits no single תנא. Next, a ברייתא limits the משנה's dispute to a case where the husband actually dies, and רבה explains that the גט works from his last moment of life, since there is no גט after death. Finally, a ברייתא begins listing the husband's rights during the in-between days, and this list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: her status in the meantime
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with two views on the woman's status before the conditional גט takes effect. The first view says she is fully like an אשת איש. רבי יוסי says she is in doubt: 'divorced and not divorced.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [She is] like a married woman in all her matters. רבי יוסי says: she is divorced and not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: We are reading the last lines of the משנה. Two opinions argue about what this woman's status is while the conditional גט is still 'waiting' to take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view (in the משנה this is רבי יהודה) treats her as completely married for now, in every way. רבי יוסי treats her as a case of doubt: maybe the גט already works, maybe not. So she gets the strict side of both statuses.

keyTerms.meaning: A married woman, forbidden to other men
In all her matters, meaning in every way
Divorced and not divorced, meaning her status is in doubt

phrases.english: Like a married woman in all her matters.
phrases.notes: In the משנה this opinion belongs to רבי יהודה; it starts just before our text.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת וְאֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: she is divorced and not divorced.
phrases.notes: He means it's a doubt. She is treated strictly both ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת וְאֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: she is fully an אשת איש in the interim. רבי יוסי: her status is a doubt, divorced and not divorced.

steps.title: ברייתא: woman seen secluded with her ex-husband
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא discusses a divorced woman seen alone with her ex-husband in the dark or sleeping with him. It says we do not suspect relations, yet we worry about זנות but not קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we also worry about קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If they saw her secluded with him in the dark, or sleeping with him at the foot of the bed, we do not worry that they did 'another thing.' We worry about זנות, but we do not worry about קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: we also worry about קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא about a divorced woman seen alone with her ex-husband. It lists what we should and should not be worried about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises two possible worries. One is זנות: they behaved immorally as an unmarried couple. The other is קידושין: he remarried her through this act, so she would need a new גט. The wording seems to contradict itself: it says we don't suspect relations, yet it worries about זנות. This sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: She was secluded (alone) with him
'Another thing,' a polite way of saying relations
Immoral relations outside of marriage
Betrothal, the act that makes a woman married
We are concerned about, or we worry about

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says 'we do not worry they did another thing' and then right away says 'we worry about זנות.' That sounds contradictory. It is exactly why the גמרא asks 'what is it saying?' in the next step.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
If they saw that she was secluded with him in the dark,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is her ex-husband, after he gave her the גט.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁיָּשְׁנָה עִמּוֹ תַּחַת מַרְגְּלוֹת הַמִּטָּה –
phrases.english: or that she slept with him at the foot of the bed –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא נִתְעַסְּקוּ בְּדָבָר אַחֵר;
phrases.english: we are not concerned that perhaps they engaged in 'another thing';
and we are concerned because of licentiousness
but we are not concerned because of betrothal.
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
We are also concerned because of betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רָאוּהָ שֶׁנִּתְיַיחֲדָה עִמּוֹ בַּאֲפֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion with a related ברייתא about a divorced woman who is later seen with her ex-husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: concern for זנות, not קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: also concern for קידושין.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since its wording seems self-contradictory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא actually means. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the ברייתא says we don't suspect relations, yet it worries about זנות. The גמרא needs a reading that makes the two parts fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A request to explain a confusing text

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the internal logic of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to read the ברייתא so that 'no concern for relations' and 'concern for זנות' don't contradict each other.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the ברייתא has two cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rereads the ברייתא as two cases. If they were seen having relations, we worry about קידושין. If he also gave her money, we treat it as payment for זנות and do not worry about קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we worry about קידושין even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This is what it means. If they saw that she had relations [with him], we worry about קידושין. If he gave her money, we worry about זנות, because we say he gave it to her as a harlot's fee, and we do not worry about קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: even in this case we worry about קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the ברייתא by splitting it into two different cases. Once it is split, it no longer contradicts itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, they were seen having relations. We worry he meant those relations as new קידושין, since relations can be a way to marry. In the second case, he also handed her money. The money makes it look like a harlot's fee, so the ת״ק sees זנות, not marriage. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה still worries that the money was given as קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; introduces a rereading of a text
She had relations
A harlot's fee, payment for forbidden relations
Even in this case

steps.whatToRemember: Relations alone lead us to worry about קידושין. Relations plus money lead the ת״ק to see זנות (a harlot's fee). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה still worries about קידושין.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said,
This is what it is saying:
If they saw that she had relations, we are concerned because of betrothal.
phrases.notes: Relations with her ex-husband could count as remarrying her.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ כְּסָפִים – חוֹשְׁשִׁין מִשּׁוּם זְנוּת,
phrases.english: If he gave her money, we are concerned because of licentiousness,
for we say: he gave it to her as her harlot's fee;
and we are not concerned because of betrothal.
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Even in this case we are concerned because of betrothal.
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the one where he gave her money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by rereading the ברייתא as two separate cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא has two cases. Relations alone: worry about קידושין. Relations plus money: ת״ק says זנות (harlot's fee), while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we worry about קידושין too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading is the basis for the next question. It tells us that 'seen having relations' is the case where everyone worries about קידושין.

steps.title: Whose view matches רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: Based on רב נחמן's reading, the גמרא asks which opinion in the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן says the dispute about needing a second גט applies only when the couple was seen having relations. If they were not seen, everyone agrees no second גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The dispute is when they saw that she had relations. But if they did not see that she had relations, everyone agrees she does not need a second גט from him. Whose view [is this]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן. It asks which side of the ברייתא his statement agrees with. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limits a known dispute to the case where relations were seen. That dispute is about whether a divorced woman who was alone with her ex-husband needs a second גט. If no relations were seen, everyone agrees there is no worry about קידושין. The גמרא now wants to match this limit to one of the views in the ברייתא as רב נחמן explained it.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
The dispute
Everyone agrees
A second bill of divorce

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is when they saw that she had relations,
phrases.notes: This is the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a divorced woman who was alone with her ex-husband: does she need a new גט?

phrases.english: but if they did not see that she had relations –

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: all agree she does not need a second bill of divorce from him?
In accordance with whom –

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב נחמן's two-case reading to ask which opinion רבי יוחנן's statement follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view in the ברייתא (the ת״ק or רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה) fits רבי יוחנן's rule that the dispute applies only when relations were seen.

steps.title: According to רב נחמן, רבי יוחנן fits everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's rule fits both opinions in the ברייתא, as רב נחמן explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is in line with everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. Using רב נחמן's reading of the ברייתא, it says רבי יוחנן's rule fits both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב נחמן's reading, the worry about קידושין only comes up when the couple was seen having relations. So if nobody saw them, both the first view and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agree there is no worry about קידושין, and no second גט is needed. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן says.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with everyone; all opinions agree

phrases.english: It is in line with everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both opinions match, because under רב נחמן's reading neither one worries about קידושין when the couple was not seen having relations.

steps.title: אביי objects that the ברייתא never mentions money
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב נחמן's reading, because it adds a case of money that the ברייתא never talks about.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Does the ברייתא teach anything about money?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב נחמן's way of reading the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן built his reading on a second case in which the man also gave the woman money. אביי points out that the ברייתא says nothing about money at all, so that reading forces a case into the text that is not there.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; he challenged it
Is anything taught? A way of saying the text does not say this
Money

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with רבי יוחנן here. He is arguing with רב נחמן's reading of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: אביי objected to it:
Does it teach anything about money?!
phrases.notes: Look back at Step 4: רב נחמן added a case where he gave her money, and אביי says the ברייתא never mentions it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ אַבָּיֵי מִידֵּי כְּסָפִים קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and attacks the reading of the ברייתא that Step 6 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's two-case reading of the ברייתא (Step 4).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading depends on a money case, but the ברייתא never mentions money.

steps.title: אביי's own reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rereads the ברייתא as a dispute about one case only: the couple was seen having relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said, this is what it means: If they saw that she had relations with him, we worry about זנות but not about קידושין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: we also worry about קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new way to read the ברייתא that does not need any money case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's reading, the whole ברייתא talks about a couple seen having relations. The first view says this counts as forbidden relations (זנות) and not as a new marriage. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we must also worry that the act made a new קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; a rereading of the text
They saw that she had relations
We worry; we take the possibility into account

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said,
This is what it means:
If they saw that she had relations with him,
we worry about forbidden relations,
but we do not worry about betrothal.
רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
We also worry about betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's reading, which Step 7 rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא had a second case involving money (רב נחמן).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא has only one case, a couple seen having relations, and the two opinions argue about whether we worry about קידושין.
steps.whyThisMatters: Under this reading, the first view does not worry about קידושין even when the couple was seen. That sets up the next question about רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Under אביי's reading, whose view does רבי יוחנן follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again which opinion in the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן's rule, now using אביי's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The dispute is when they saw she had relations, but if they did not see it, everyone agrees she does not need a second גט from him. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as in Step 5 again, now on top of אביי's reading. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that when the couple was seen having relations, there is a real dispute about needing a second גט, so someone must worry about קידושין. In אביי's reading, the first view never worries about קידושין, even when they were seen. So the question is which opinion רבי יוחנן's rule can fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
The dispute
A second bill of divorce

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow, what was said by

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
The dispute is when they saw that she had relations,
phrases.notes: This is the dispute from Step 5 about whether she needs a second גט.

phrases.english: but if they did not see that she had relations,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: everyone agrees she does not need a second גט from him?
Whose view is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes אביי's new reading and tests it against רבי יוחנן's rule, just as Step 5 tested רב נחמן's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the ברייתא, as אביי reads it, matches רבי יוחנן's rule that the dispute applies only when the couple was seen having relations.

steps.title: Under אביי's reading, רבי יוחנן fits רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 9: with אביי's reading, רבי יוחנן's rule matches רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It fits the opinion of רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked. Using אביי's reading of the ברייתא, רבי יוחנן's rule matches רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's reading, the whole ברייתא talks only about a couple who was seen having relations. The תנא קמא says there is no concern about קידושין even then, while רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says that in that case we do worry about קידושין. רבי יוחנן says the need for a second גט comes up only when they were seen, and that matches רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the שאלה of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under אביי's reading, רבי יוחנן's rule fits רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, not the תנא קמא.

steps.title: רבא asks what the word 'also' means
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's reading: if that reading were right, the word 'אף' (also) in רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's statement would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: If so, what does 'also' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's reading of the ברייתא. He points to one word, 'אף', that does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' means 'in addition to the worry already mentioned,' which is זנות. In אביי's reading, both views are talking about the same act of relations. If we worry that it was קידושין, then it was a marriage and not זנות, so it makes no sense to worry about both 'also.'

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; a strong challenge
If so, meaning if your reading is right
Also, even; a word that signals adding something more

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
If so, what is the meaning of "also"?
phrases.notes: He's pointing to the word 'also' in רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's line: 'there is also a concern about קידושין.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, מַאי ״אַף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of אביי that made the answer in step 10 possible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In אביי's reading, 'אף' would mean worrying about קידושין in addition to זנות for the same act. But if the act may have been קידושין, there is nothing to worry about as זנות, so 'also' does not fit.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא: concern even when they were not seen
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says even if the couple was not seen having relations, we still worry about קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what it means. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says: Even if they did not see that she had relations, we are concerned about קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading of the ברייתא so that the word 'also' fits. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה goes further and worries even when nobody saw the couple having relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'also' has a clear job. It means that even in the easier case, where they were not seen, רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה still worries about קידושין. The תנא קמא, in this reading, does not worry about קידושין at all, even when they were seen. That is why step 14 says רבי יוחנן fits neither of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier reading for a new one
This is what it is saying; introduces a rereading
They did not see that she had relations
We are concerned, we take it into account

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Even if they did not see that she had relations,
one is concerned because of betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge by replacing אביי's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so the word 'אף' fits
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי read רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה as worrying about קידושין only when the couple was seen having relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה worries about קידושין even when they were not seen. That is the meaning of 'also'.

steps.title: Whom does רבי יוחנן fit under רבא's reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again which opinion matches רבי יוחנן's rule, now using רבא's new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion fits what רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The dispute is only when they saw that she had relations, but if they did not see it, everyone agrees she does not need a second גט from him? Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the same question a third time, now testing רבי יוחנן's rule against רבא's reading. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that when no one saw them, everyone agrees no second גט is needed. But in רבא's reading, רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה worries about קידושין even when they were not seen. So רבי יוחנן's rule can no longer fit him, and the גמרא must find another match.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does it follow?
The dispute
Everyone agrees
She does not need a second גט from him

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same question as steps 5 and 9, and it is asked again on purpose. Each time the ברייתא is read differently, the answer to 'whom does רבי יוחנן fit?' can change.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this
that Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The dispute is when they saw that she had relations,
phrases.notes: The dispute here is the one between בית שמאי and בית הלל about whether she needs a second גט.

phrases.english: but if they did not see that she had relations,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט?
phrases.english: everyone agrees that she does not need a bill of divorce from him?
In accordance with whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's new reading from step 12 to ask the same question asked in steps 5 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the ברייתא, as רבא reads it, matches רבי יוחנן's rule that everyone agrees no second גט is needed when the couple was not seen?

steps.title: With רבא's reading, רבי יוחנן's rule fits no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that, using רבא's reading of the ברייתא, רבי יוחנן's rule does not match any single תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not like any one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13: using רבא's reading, רבי יוחנן's rule does not fit any one opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, the תנא קמא is not worried about קידושין even when the couple was seen having relations. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה worries even when they were not seen. רבי יוחנן's rule sits in between: the question of a second גט comes up only when they were seen, and not otherwise. So it matches neither side.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like any one (of the opinions)
We worry that קידושין may have happened
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Under אביי's reading, רבי יוחנן fits רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה. Under רבא's reading, he fits no single תנא; his position is a middle view.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יוחנן's rule is rejected. It only means that, in רבא's reading, it is a middle position that no single תנא in the ברייתא holds.

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with any one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With רבא's reading, רבי יוחנן's rule matches no single תנא, because it falls between the two opinions.

steps.title: The woman's status during the in-between days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's argument about what the woman's status is before her sick husband dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is her status during those days? רבי יהודה says: she is like a married woman in every way. רבי יוסי says: she is divorced and not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a line from the משנה. That line asks about the woman's status during the days before her husband dies. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband gave a גט and said 'if I die from this illness.' Until he dies, nobody knows whether the גט will take effect. רבי יהודה treats her as fully married for now. רבי יוסי treats her status as uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: During those days, before the husband dies
A married woman
Divorced and not divorced, so her status is in doubt

phrases.english: What is she during those days?
phrases.notes: The days between getting the גט ('if I die from this illness') and the husband's death.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: like a married woman in all her matters,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת וְאֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: divorced and not divorced.
phrases.notes: He means it is unclear whether she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: during the in-between days she is a full אשת איש. רבי יוסי: her status is in doubt.

steps.title: The argument applies only if he dies
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that this argument only matters if the husband actually dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: provided that he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a condition: the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי only applies if the husband ends up dying. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he recovers, the condition was never met and the גט never works, so nothing needs deciding. The question about her status only matters when he dies and the גט might take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, only if

phrases.english: It was taught: provided that he dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the case of the משנה's argument quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument about her in-between status applies only if the husband dies from that illness.

steps.title: A divorce cannot take effect after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a גט can work 'when he dies,' since we hold there is no גט after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he dies, it becomes a גט?! But we hold that there is no גט after death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 16: if the גט only works once he dies, it would take effect after death, and a גט cannot do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A marriage ends by itself when the husband dies, so a גט has nothing left to end afterward. 'Provided that he dies' sounds like the גט kicks in at death, which looks impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, it is established for us
A גט cannot take effect after death

phrases.english: And when he dies, it is a bill of divorce?!
But don't we hold
that there is no bill of divorce after death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the condition taught in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'provided that he dies.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גט only works when he dies, it would take effect after death. That contradicts the accepted rule that there is no גט after death.

steps.title: He meant the last moment of his life
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the husband said the גט should work 'from the time I am still in the world,' meaning just before death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: this is where he says, 'from the time that I am in the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge from step 17. The husband made the גט take effect while he was still alive, at his last moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט does not take effect after death. It takes effect a moment before death, while the marriage still exists. His death only shows that the condition was met.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time I am (still) in the world, meaning the last moment of life

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a deathbed גט can work at all: it must be set for the last moment of life, not for the time after death.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Where he says: 'from the time that I am in the world.'
phrases.notes: He means the last moment he is still alive, right before he dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בְּאוֹמֵר מֵעֵת שֶׁאֲנִי בָּעוֹלָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the husband's exact wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט takes effect at death, which would be after death and impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband set the גט for the last moment of his life, so it works while he is still alive.

steps.title: The husband's rights during the in-between days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins listing the rights the husband keeps during the days before he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: during the in-between days, her husband is entitled to what she finds, to her earnings, and to cancel her vows; and he inherits from her,
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא starts listing what the husband still has during the days before his death. The list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item on the list is a right a husband normally has over his wife. Because the גט has not yet taken effect, he keeps these rights during the waiting period.

keyTerms.meaning: The days in between (the גט and his death)
What she finds (lost objects)
Her earnings from her work
Canceling her vows
He inherits from her

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The days in between –
phrases.notes: Between getting the גט and the husband's death.

phrases.english: her husband is entitled to what she finds,
and to her earnings,
and to annulling her vows;
and he inherits from her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with practical details about the in-between days discussed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the in-between days, the husband keeps his normal rights: what she finds, her earnings, canceling her vows, and inheriting from her (the list continues).
